#6591. 25 Midwestern Thanksgiving Recipes That Bring The Nostalgia (& The Flavor)

Even nicer than Midwest nice (and that's saying something!).

My holidays were split between regions growing up. We spent Thanksgiving at my dad’s side, and Christmas with my mom’s. With my mom’s Alabama and Texas roots and my dad's Missouri and Kansas roots, that meant that Christmas dinner was a Southern affair and Thanksgiving was a Midwestern feast. Both holiday spreads had a fair amount of overlap of dishes (casseroles galore), but I have to say: A classic Midwest Thanksgiving has a special place in my heart.

What makes a Midwest Thanksgiving, you may ask? All of the classics are present, plus a few surprising favorites that, in my house, no holiday is complete without. We think beyond the turkey, sometimes skip mashed potatoes for a cheesy casserole, and have to be careful not to fill up on all the rolls (butter and honey better be on the table). Ready to celebrate Midwest-style? Here are some recipes that your holiday won’t be complete without:

Made with canned pineapple, pistachio pudding, and Cool Whip, this retro crowd-pleasing dessert “salad” will take you straight back to the ’70s with just one bite. It’s the perfect recipe to throw together if you don’t have a ton of time, but you need to take something to that potluck or family gathering.

Thanksgiving is equally about food and football, so this tailgate-inspired stuffing is a no-brainer. Filled with beer cheese sauce and topped with crispy bacon, this twist on the classic holiday side is so irresistible, it’ll be gone long before halftime of that first Thanksgiving Day game.

It takes less than than 5 minutes to pour some pepper jelly over cream cheese and place some crackers around. These bites are slightly more elevated without many more steps. It’s for those that want to feel like they are putting some effort into their appetizer without it being difficult or time-consuming.

Don't be fooled by the name—the only thing deathly about this casserole is how absolutely delicious it is. This cheesy, creamy casserole is a staple at every holiday in my Kansas home, and Thanksgiving is no exception. Yes, we often have mashed potatoes too.

For this recipe, we ditched canned cream of mushroom soup and went for fresh instead. It's not how my mom makes it, but trust me—by sautéing mushrooms with sliced onion in butter, you're building a base with some serious depth of flavor. Cook the mushrooms enough that they get a little caramelized, and you'll really be good to go.

No matter the holiday, one thing is for sure: Deviled eggs will be making an appearance. Variations are always welcome (looking at you, harissa deviled eggs), but if grandpa is going to have a happy Thanksgiving, then this classic recipe better be present.

Strawberry pretzel tart, AKA strawberry pretzel salad, might sound a little strange, but trust us—it strikes the perfect balance of whimsical and classic, sweet and salty. The pretzel crust proves to be an ideal complement to the rich cream cheese layer and the sweet strawberries with their Jell-O glaze.

Turkey usually rules the roost at Thanksgiving, but it's not the only centerpiece present at many Midwestern holiday tables. Depending on how many family members are coming, my family has been known to prepare a turkey and a ham—it's the best of both worlds!

We’re certainly not opposed to roasted Brussels sprouts, but we also love giving them the traditional Thanksgiving treatment—plenty of butter, cream, and cheese. This method upgrades even the most humble vegetables while still allowing them to be the star of the show.

This sweet party dip is the perfect way to add that little extra something to your fruit spread, but your dipping options don't stop there! With just 5 minutes of prep, this is the easiest dessert that any party will be thankful for. Plus, you can easily make it ahead and travel with it, making it an ideal potluck recipe.

These Thanksgiving potato skins are piled high with leftovers, but they’re so good, they just might deserve a place in your holiday spread. The hollowed-out potatoes are an excellent vessel for extra-creamy mashed potatoes, stuffing, turkey, and dollops of cranberry sauce.

Essentially, this is chicken Alfredo, but with a few extra decadent add-ins, like cream cheese, garlic, and punchy spices like nutmeg and black pepper. When you’re craving the classic but have to serve a crowd, this is the recipe you should make.

A cheese ball is peak party appetizer nostalgia, and these cheese ball bites are here to put a new, shareable twist on the classic. They’re so simple to make, only require a handful of ingredients, and are super versatile based on what you have on hand.

I'll clarify that when I say stuffing, I'm actually referring to dressing. Traditional stuffing should be stuffed inside the turkey and cooked in there, but in my family, we've always called it stuffing. By cooking your stuffing in a baking dish, you get crunchy, buttery pieces of bread on top and soft, bread pudding-esque pieces underneath.

What’s the best kind of potato? A loaded baked potato, of course. With this in mind, we combined the two superstar spuds into one glorious dish. In it, light, airy mashed potatoes are topped with all of the classic baked potato fillings—cheddar cheese, chives, bacon, and sour cream—for a dish that truly embodies the best of both worlds.

Most sweet potato casseroles have only marshmallows or pecans. Don't even think about making this mistake. Topping with a pecan streusel and then marshmallows helps this Thanksgiving casserole stand out above all the rest.

If you’re not into creamy, melty macaroni and cheese with a wildly satisfying cheese-pull, then you might want to find another mac recipe. Sorry, but this slow-cooker macaroni and cheese is just too darn dreamy.

Step aside, all other casseroles—corn is not to be overlooked on the holiday table. If you prefer, drained and rinsed canned corn can be used instead of frozen, and you could substitute more milk in for the heavy cream. The finished casserole won't be quite as decadent, but it will still be delicious.

Deviled eggs are great, but when you have them for every holiday, it just makes sense to change them up sometimes. These are our new obsession

If green beans dressed up as cheesy garlic bread, then they would become these Parmesan roasted green beans. Tossed in garlic and black pepper and showered with cheese, this simply irresistible side dish will steal the spotlight at every holiday table.

This sweet party dip is the perfect way to add that little extra something to your fruit spread, but your dipping options don't stop there! With just 5 minutes of prep, this is the easiest dessert that any party will be thankful for.

#6590. 13 Pairs of Gloves to Keep Your Digits Toasty All Winter Long

Every product was carefully curated by an Esquire editor. We may earn a commission from these links. Here’s how we test products and why you should trust us.

Don’t overlook your cold-weather style practicalities.

There are few winter experiences more miserable than stepping outside with bare hands and realizing, too late, that your fingers have stopped working. First they’re freezing, then they’re numb, and before long your skin feels dry and rough and beyond the help of any hand lotion.

But honestly? Gloves can be annoying, too. Some turn a quick phone check into a whole production; others are so bulky you might as well be wearing oven mitts. The best winter gloves keep your hands warm without making your fingers useless—and look good while they’re at it. We’ve rounded up our favorites, from waterproof, windproof pairs built for rough weather to stylish options that still keep your hands nice and toasty. And yes, plenty have touchscreen-compatible fingertips so you can still call and text (and play the Wordle). See our favorite pairs below.

These luxurious leather gloves come from Overland, the brand behind some of our favorite coats. The smooth leather looks very polished, so these gloves can be dressed up if you want, but they go just as well with a casual outfit. They’re also quite durable and are naturally water-repellant, and the cashmere lining adds warmth on the inside.

Commerce Editor Luke Guillory loves these merino wool-lined deerskin gloves from Geier Gloves, a brand that has been making leather products in the U.S. for almost a century. Since the brand specializes in leather, you can bet the deerskin on these gloves is of the highest quality, and the wool lining is very nice, too. Geier also makes a lot of wor, driving, and motorcycle gloves, so you know they’re the real deal. The black and brown colorways look quite polished, but the natural and saddle leather options are also great.

If you want a nice luxurious pair of cashmere gloves, go with these ones from Sunspel. Lately, I’ve been wearing these gloves, which were knitted in Scotland from super soft pure cashmere. The brand has been perfecting the craft for over 150 years, so you can trust that these are the best of the best. It’s basically like enveloping your hands in a cozy blanket. For a full set, get the brand’s cashmere hat and scarf.

These Canada Goose gloves are basically the equivalent of wearing a puffer jacket on your hands. With heavy-duty, long rib-knit cuffs for extra protection and 750-fill-power down on the inside, your hands will stay warm and dry without their mobility being super impacted by something extra bulky. Note that these have a touchscreen-compatible index finger but not thumb.

Wool-blend gloves are as handsome as any of the very best sweaters in your rotation. Even though the outside is made from knit material, the insulated interior will keep your hands warm and dry during your next epic snowball fight. They’re also thin enough to layer under another pair of gloves if it’s really freezing outside.

When it comes to gloves, there’s one brand I’ve trusted for years, and that’s Smartwool. Their gloves are warm without being bulky, and mine have lasted for years. Having a warm pair of gloves that actually does its job well is even more important for my boyfriend, who has Raynaud’s and needs extra protection for his hands, and the gloves he relies on year after year? Also Smartwool. These new fleece gloves from the brand have extra insulation on the back to provide serious warmth, and they’re also functional with touchscreen-compatible pads on the thumbs and index fingers. Sure, they’re a little expensive for fleece gloves at $68—but if you don’t need the extra insulation, you can try the regular Active Fleece Gloves for $48.

If all you need is a solid pair of knit gloves and you’re not looking to spend a fortune, look no further than Uniqlo. The brand’s Heattech knit gloves are soft and warm and have effective touchscreen-compatible fingertips. They also come in 11 fun colors, so you might as well get a couple pairs for yourself—and they make a great holiday gift for literally anyone.

You already know we love Barbour’s waxed canvas jackets, so it’s no surprise we’re also a fan of the brand’s stylish, preppy gloves. These leather-palmed gloves have a cotton tartan face for a cool contrast and wool lining on the inside for extra warmth—and they’re waterproof, so you can break them out no matter what’s going on with the weather. Pair these with the Barbour Beaufort jacket for an iconic look.

Knit gloves are great when it comes to keeping warm, but they’re not the best when it’s raining or snowing. No one wants a pair of soaking gloves (that probably make your hands feel even colder). Enter these waterproof gloves from the brand that brought you the famous Bean Boots. With a waterproof nylon exterior and a down fill, they’ll keep rain and show out while keeping your hands warm. Note that some say the fingers are long, so consider that when choosing a size.

When you’re stuck in a blizzard or your location is prone to unpredictable weather, you’ll need something a little more heavy duty. REI’s weatherproof gore-tex gloves will give your hands the protection they need. They’re also essentially a two-in-one: The removable fleece liners can be used on their own or with the weatherproof outers as an extra layer of warmth.

Naadam’s famous cashmere sweater is one of our favorite pieces of winter clothing and one of our go-to gifts for the holidays, birthdays, Valentine’s Day, etc. The brand makes a matching pair of soft cashmere gloves, which come in 13 colors and are under $100. A genius gift idea? Get them the sweater with a matching pair of gloves, and they’ll wear both all winter long.

If you want that classic Sherlock Holmes leather glove look, you have lots of choices. But if you don’t want to spend a ton on a pair, get these $60 gloves from Quince. Not only do they have a nice leather exterior in either brown or black, they also have a cashmere lining on the inside.

On the high end of the high end, Gucci has a gorgeous luxury pair of leather gloves with the brand’s signature horsebit on the wrist for a fun little detail. Made from leather and silk, these are soft, smooth, and very stylish.

You’re a bit more nostalgic when it comes to love once Venus enters Scorpio on December 4. You might find yourself fantasizing about ex-lovers or even glossing over the bad and romanticizing the past in some way. This season can also remind you how much you benefit from spending some time alone every now and then. Slowing down and reconnecting with yourself will help strengthen your relationship with your inner voice and intuition, as well.

You’re learning important, personal news once Mercury enters your sign on December 6. You could have a bright idea or new goal you want to set for yourself. This also puts you in a mindset to focus on yourself and your needs, which can bring about progress on your personal goals. You might also have important personal news you want to share with others, letting people catch a glimpse of who you really are and what matters most to you.

A New Moon, in your sign, on December 8 helps you recommit to yourself. This is your yearly permission slip to forgive yourself, release old baggage, and show up differently. You’re ready to show up more authentically by focusing on the people, projects, and hobbies that light you up. Who and what makes you feel most like yourself? Spend more time investing in those areas of your life. This energy also brings new beginnings into your world, and you can use this momentum however you see fit.

You’re setting firm boundaries in your romantic life when Saturn stations direct in Aries on December 10. You might need to end a fling or address an uncomfortable topic. This can also give you the push you need to make a commitment and go all-in. You’re also feeling ready to stick with a certain hobby or project and take it more seriously. You have the structure necessary to pour consistent effort into your vision or whatever brings you joy.

The creative inspiration you’ve been waiting for arrives when Neptune stations direct in Aries on December 12. If you’ve felt stuck dealing with writer’s block or some form of stagnant creative energy, that starts to subside. This can also serve up reality checks regarding your romantic life. Have you been putting someone on a pedestal? Have you been prioritizing your desire and pleasure in authentic ways? It’s time to throw away the rose-colored glasses.

Conversations feel profound and healing when Jupiter stations retrograde in Leo, also on December 12. You might learn news that changes your perspective or opens you up to new possibilities. This new information might take some time to integrate. This energy is also wonderful for going back to school, picking up a writing project, or booking some travel. You will learn more and more through lived experience over the coming months.

The Sun enters Capricorn and the Winter Solstice takes place on December 21, encouraging you to check in with your current priorities. How are you expending your time, energy, and resources? You might gain more attention for your talents over the coming weeks and with the extra attention comes extra pressure. This can also help you refine and reflect on who and what you’re focused on in your life. Does it feel truly meaningful and fulfilling?

A Full Moon in Cancer on December 23 puts you in touch with some emotions you thought you already sorted through. This can drudge up the past, which can feel jarring and overwhelming. This can help you confront and integrate some of your shadow side by feeling, processing, and being accountable in new ways. There might also be conversations around shared resources and finances, or reciprocity in certain relationships, contracts, or obligations in your life. If you feel underappreciated, now is the time to speak up.

The month wraps up with Mercury moving into Capricorn on December 25, helping you make important financial decisions. You might start applying for jobs or feel ready to set firmer boundaries at work or ask for a raise. You might also want to invest in yourself in some way—whether it’s buying a new coffee machine, booking a massage, or finding more time to thrift on the weekends. You know you can’t take your money with you when you leave this place so you might as well enjoy it.

#6587. A New Azzedine Alaïa Retrospective Goes Beyond the Bandage Dress

The Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco examines the great couturier’s legacy

The bandage dress. The zipper dress. The perforated leather. The jersey hoods. The peplummed chemises. Azzedine Alaïa’s designs may not look so radical now, but almost 50 years ago, he changed the collective tide of fashion. The bandage dress is perhaps the most pervasive bit of his legacy, and it is emblematic of how the late French-Tunisian designer ushered in a new body-conscious silhouette in the ’80s, one made possible by technological innovations in materials that sculpted without any rigid, waist-cinching structure.

Alaïa’s designs “were completely shocking” to the public at the time, recounts Laura Camerlengo, curator in charge of costume and textile arts at the Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco. She has spent the past four years developing a new exhibition titled “Azzedine Alaïa: Sculpting Fashion,” the first major U.S. retrospective dedicated to the work of the famed couturier. It opened November 21.

Born in 1935 in Tunis, Alaïa first trained as a sculptor, a background evident in his body of work. In 1956, he decamped to Paris to pursue fashion full-time. After a brief internship at the house of Christian Dior, he worked under Guy Laroche for less than two years before taking on his own private clients, then launching his own atelier in the late ’70s. From there, he built the house we know today. His obsession with construction and material innovation allowed him to both celebrate and liberate the female form. He passed away in late 2017 at the age of 82.

Camerlengo first encountered Alaïa’s work as an assistant on the “Patrick Kelly Runway of Love” exhibition that the Philadelphia Museum of Art organized in 2014. “I was intrigued by how many of the new designers in Paris at this time were being supported by US consumers and retailers,” she says. After ascending to her new position in San Francisco years later, she cold-emailed Olivier Saillard, director of the Azzedine Alaïa Foundation in Paris. He was intrigued, and the two began working together on the exhibition almost immediately.

The exhibition focuses on 80 garments from across Alaïa’s celebrated career, divided over a series of archetypes—the bandage dresses, sculptures and shapes, black and white, silhouettes and suiting, and construction and craftsmanship—to explore how his design aesthetic evolved. Interspersed are designs worn by devotees like Tina Turner, Grace Jones, and Rihanna. One final gallery highlights his personal collections of the work of designers he most admired, like Christian Dior and Charles James.

Ahead, Camerlengo speaks to Bazaar about curating the new exhibition, contextualizing Alaïa’s work in today’s fashion landscape, and his enduring legacy.

The exhibition is not chronological. We look at a series of Alaïa’s archetypes like the bandage dress to explore how his design aesthetic evolved over the course of his career. He often himself said that he didn’t want to conform to seasonal trends; he was more interested in the evolution of his designs. And so the gallery shows a mix of objects dating from the 1980s to his final collection in 2017, and they’re largely grouped by type.

When you come in, you are greeted by Grace Jones, as we say, and the seminal purple hooded bandage dress from the fashion Oscars [a French event held in 1985]. As you move through, you’ll see a selection of the zipper dresses, the chiffon gowns, and other works that tie into some of the other themes. In each space, we mix the time periods. And that was something Alaïa himself often said. [He had a running joke that he didn’t know his own age.] He often said he was “as old as the pharaohs.” Basically, time was a construct for him.

That’s a great word for it. We could think of the popularity of the Japanese fashion designers who obscured women’s bodies with their voluminous styles. We could think of the suiting of the period. The 1970s is this period of workplace equality. Women are wearing suits in the style of masculine dress, but that also means they're obscuring their bodies. And then we can think of pop culture. I always think of Diane Keaton’s Annie Hall in 1977.

Some of the individuals I interviewed for my catalog text who were retailers in San Francisco at the time described Alaïa's designs as being like a whiplash. It was a complete 180 from the styles that they had gotten used to over the past decade, which also includes the rise of T-shirts and jeans for women as a mode of dress.

So here you have these very sexy, very form-fitting clothes. And part of the Alaïa aesthetic, as I see it, is the reclamation of the gaze. Rather than women being passively looked at—usually by men—they are instead commanding their own agency. As you said, it was completely earth-shattering and very shocking at the time.

Azzedine Alaïa was one of the few couturiers who could work completely by the methods of tailoring and by draping, start to finish, from the initial concept to the final product. I did not fully appreciate his tailoring and the suits he constructed beforehand. We have a selection of them in a gallery of the exhibition, and their construction is absolutely incredible. The way they fit the body, the way they uplift and empower women through cloth—again, very antithetical to what we saw in the decades prior in the 1970s. These are very form-fitting, tailored at the waist, but they have soft feminine touches as well that give you this interesting mix of femininity and strength at the same time.

Very important. We talk in the first gallery about how women, speaking generally, were the architects of his life. He learned to sew from his sister, who was working for a seamstress. He was encouraged by a local midwife in Tunisia to go to school at the Institute of Fine Arts. She helped him forge his papers to read 16—he was only 15 at the time. He learned his skills, not in formal training, but from women in Tunisia.

And then his early work was supported by a lot of leading figures of international society, including various Rothschilds, the French performer Arletty, the Swedish American actress Greta Garbo, and that's all before he even started to work formally under his own label in the 1980s. Of course, in the 1980s, he adopts Naomi Campbell, who becomes his protégé. He has close relationships with Grace Jones and Tina Turner. They were hugely important to him. In the exhibition, the clear invisible mounts that we use are actually based on the body of Naomi Campbell.

Probably the Grace Jones bandage dress from the fashion Oscars in 1985. Not only is it the progression of the bandage dress style that he experiments with throughout the course of the 1980s, but it represents a key moment in his career where he receives two very high accolades as part of the fashion Oscars and he’s recognized for his genius.

As far as the designs themselves, I think we would consider the bandage dress, for example, an iconic symbol of late 20th- and 21st-century fashion developed by Azzedine Alaïa, but of course iterated upon extensively. We've seen surges and resurgences in its popularity ever since.

And then as far as the landscape of the broader fashion system, Alaïa was someone who really eschewed seasonal calendars and trends. He was unconcerned with making things for the market. He often wanted to just produce clothes and share them when he felt they were ready. So I think his method of working foreshadows some of the conversations we’re having now about the overproduction of fashion and the overconsumption of fashion, even the detrimental environmental impacts that we see connected to it. He was really a forerunner, in a sense, to question the fashion system.

You can see how he really studied the construction of other garments and then adapted it in his own way in his designs. For example, he admired the work of Charles James, the great American fashion designer who was able to manipulate fabric to achieve weightless volume. And you see in Alaïa's own collections as he continues in his career, he does radial tucks and pleating to also get a certain amount of weightless volume in some of his gowns, very much in the spirit of James.

I hope our visitors appreciate the artistry of his work, first and foremost, and also the importance of handcraftsmanship. We are increasingly in an age of technology, especially with the rise of AI. What he created by his own hand is something that we can really marvel at.

#6586. Popeyes Beat KFC In My Chicken Sandwich Showdown—But Can It Take Down Chick-fil-A?

The chicken sandwich wars are far from over.

Few fast food rivalries are as competitive as the battle for the best chicken sandwich. And while plenty of chains have introduced their own versions over the years, Chick-fil-A and Popeyes remain two of the biggest names in the conversation.

In my previous chicken sandwich showdown, I put KFC and Popeyes head-to-head to see which chain served the better sandwich. Popeyes ultimately came out on top, thanks to its bold seasoning, crispy breading, and well-balanced toppings. This time, I’m putting Popeyes up against one of its biggest competitors: Chick-fil-A.

Chick-fil-A has built its reputation around a simple, flavorful chicken sandwich that doesn’t need much to stand out. Popeyes, meanwhile, practically broke the internet when it introduced its now-famous chicken sandwich in 2019, sparking a fast food frenzy.

I ordered each chain’s original chicken sandwich to compare flavor, texture, juiciness, and overall balance. Both have their strengths, but only one can move on as my favorite.

Chick-fil-A’s Original Chicken Sandwich keeps things simple with a breaded chicken fillet, pickles, and a toasted bun.

Chick-fil-A’s chicken is so recognizable for a reason. The seasoning and brine give the fillet a savory, slightly tangy flavor that’s hard to beat, while the crispy breading contrasts nicely with the juicy chicken. The pickles also do their job, adding just enough acidity and crunch to balance out the richness.

My biggest complaint is that I wanted a little more from the sandwich. Compared to other fast food chicken sandwiches I’ve tried, many of which come with some type of sauce, Chick-fil-A’s original feels a bit plain. The chicken has enough flavor to stand on its own, but I think a little mayo or another sauce would have made the overall sandwich even better.

Still, there’s something to be said for a chicken sandwich that relies almost entirely on the quality and flavor of the chicken itself.

Popeyes’ Classic Chicken Sandwich features a breaded chicken fillet, pickles, mayo, and a toasted brioche bun. The sandwich that practically broke the internet when it launched in 2019 still lives up to the hype.

I’ve had this sandwich before where the chicken was slightly dry in spots, but thankfully that wasn’t the case this time. The fillet was juicy, flavorful, and incredibly well-seasoned. The breading had a satisfying crunch, and the bold, savory flavor made me want to keep going back for another bite.

The mayo was another important part of the sandwich, adding a tangy creaminess that complemented the chicken without overpowering it. Paired with the crisp pickles, it helped balance out the richness of the fried fillet.

I also really appreciated the proportions. The soft brioche bun held everything together without overwhelming the chicken, and each bite had a good balance of meat, breading, sauce, and pickles.

While Popeyes might not always deliver the most consistently juicy chicken, everything came together particularly well during this taste test. Between the seasoning, crispy breading, and well-balanced toppings, it’s easy to understand why this sandwich became such a phenomenon in the first place.

Popeyes already managed to beat KFC in my previous comparison, and after going up against Chick-fil-A, it’s keeping its winning streak alive.

Chick-fil-A arguably has the more distinctive chicken flavor, thanks to its savory, slightly tangy seasoning. But when I’m ordering a chicken sandwich, I want the entire thing to work together, and that’s where Popeyes has the advantage.

Chick-fil-A is still a great option, especially if you prefer a simpler sandwich that lets the chicken do most of the work. But after trying both, Popeyes delivered the better overall experience. With two wins under its belt, Popeyes is proving to be a pretty tough sandwich to beat.

If you’re a fan of The Hunting Wives, chances are you’re probably invested in the on-screen affair between Brittany Snow and Malin Akerman’s characters, Sophie and Margo. But off screen, both actresses are happily in relationships—Akerman with her husband of eight years, Jack Donnelly, and Snow with new fiancé Hunter Moreno.

Snow announced the engagement news on a November 19 appearance on The Drew Barrymore Show, when Barrymore asked her directly, “Are you recently engaged?” The Hunting Wives star replied, “You know what? The costars then playfully admitted they jokingly refer to the cast’s boyfriends and husbands as “The Hunting Husbands.”

So, who is Snow’s fiancé, Hunter Moreno? Ahead, everything to know about the creative and their relationship.

Based in Los Angeles, Moreno began his career directing and filming YouTube videos for influencers before expanding into music, directing videos for artists including Dasha, Charlie Puth, Ava Max, and Machine Gun Kelly. Mental health advocacy is also important to Snow, who co-founded September Letters in 2020. The letter-writing platform, which has partnered with the Mental Health Coalition, aims to help end the stigma surrounding mental health.

Moreno and Snow were first publicly linked in October 2024, when they were photographed kissing while walking through New York City. During a 2026 appearance on The Drew Barrymore Show, Snow confirmed that the two began dating during the filming of The Hunting Wives’ first season, which began in 2024.

On March 28, 2026, Snow made their relationship Instagram official—though it was slyly packed into a massive carousel post. Amongst the photos from her birthday celebration in the desert were two photos of Snow and Moreno, a mirror selfie and a photo of the two posing with her dog.

Though Moreno’s Instagram is mostly dedicated to his professional work, in September, he uploaded a carousel of photos taken of Snow while traveling from Italy to France.

Rumors of an engagement first sparked between Snow and Moreno in November 2025, when a video shared by DeuxMoi showed Claire Danes chatting with Snow on a red carpet and seemingly congratulating her on her engagement. “You’re engaged?!” Danes exclaimed during the exchange. “You know what? For the first time, I’m gonna tell you, I’m gonna tell you. Yes, we’re engaged, yeah,” Snow said when Barrymore asked her directly. “I haven’t said it before. It’s okay. It’s not that big of a secret. I mean, like, who cares?”

#6582. A Complete Timeline of Justin and Hailey Bieber’s Relationship

The singer and supermodel-turned-skin care mogul are one of Hollywood’s leading power couples.

Justin Bieber and Hailey Baldwin dated on and off long before they became husband and wife. Hailey first met Justin in the late aughts, and they eventually struck up a casual romance.

Though they decided to keep it out of the public eye, this didn’t stop fans from obsessing over their relationship. After a breakup and surprise reconciliation-turned-whirlwind engagement two years later, Justin officially made Hailey his Mrs. during a September 2018 New York City courthouse ceremony. They got married in front of friends and family in a more formal wedding a year later. In May 2024, they announced they were expecting their first child. They welcomed their son, Jack, in August 2024.

From their highly publicized South Carolina nuptials to their adjustment to parenthood, here’s the couple’s full history and how their relationship has evolved.

Hailey has her father, Stephen, to thank for introducing her to her future husband. There’s even footage of their first meeting, which took place backstage at The Today Show. Hailey and Justin—then in their teens—shared a brief handshake and the rest, as they say, is history.

Chaperoned by her father yet again, Hailey attended the New York City premiere of Justin’s documentary Never Say Never. Later that month, Justin confirmed his relationship with Selena Gomez when the couple made their red carpet debut at Vanity Fair’s Oscar After Party.

Hailey officially declared herself a member of the Jelena fan club. The model took to Twitter, sharing her support for the couple. “I don’t care what anyone says but Justin Bieber and Selena Gomez together is the definition of a teenage dream! #word,” Hailey wrote.

After calling it quits with Gomez, Justin was photographed attending church services at Hillsong alongside Hailey and fellow supermodel Kendall Jenner. It wasn’t long before fans began speculating that Hailey and Justin were an item.

Hailey denied any romantic connection between her and Justin. She set the record straight during an interview with E!. “I’ve known [Justin] since I was like 13—and we’ve just been good friends over the years,” Hailey said. “We have just stayed close, and there’s nothing more to it than that.”

Justin backed up Hailey’s statement in an Instagram post. The singer shared a snap of himself and Hailey, writing, “I’m super single and this is my good friend u would know otherwise.”

Hailey joined Justin and his family on vacation in Anguilla, fueling rumors that their friendship was actually something more.

Justin made his romance with Hailey Instagram official. Shortly after New Year’s Day, he shared a photo of them kissing.

Hailey and Justin revealed that their relationship was casual. “We are not an exclusive couple,” Hailey told E!. Meanwhile, in an interview with GQ, Justin called Hailey “someone I really love,” but he added that he didn’t “want to be held down by anything.”

Hailey and Justin ended their brief fling. According to People, Justin also unfollowed Hailey on Instagram amid his new relationship with Sofia Richie.

Following their split, Hailey and Justin completely lost touch for almost two years. In 2020, Hailey shared her thoughts on their time apart: “Our lives seemed to be going in very different directions,” she told ELLE. “I actually think—now that I look back at it being married—that it was a good thing for the two of us, very healthy.”

During Justin and Hailey’s rift, the singer rekindled his romance with Gomez in November 2017. However, by March 2018, Jelena was over for good.

Hailey revealed that she was speaking to Justin again. “We went through a long period of time when we weren’t friends,” she told The Times U.K.. “We’ve moved past that.”

Justin and Hailey appeared as if they were back together. After sharing some PDA at a religious conference, they were spotted together at LIV nightclub in Miami. Just days later, they were photographed holding hands and kissing in New York City.

After rumors of the couple’s engagement began to swirl, Justin confirmed the news on Instagram. He posted two portraits with his new fiancée and penned a lengthy caption devoted to her. “Hailey I am soooo in love with everything about you,” he wrote. “So committed to spending my life getting to know every single part of you.”

Hailey joined the love fest, tweeting, “Not sure what I did in life to deserve such happiness but I am so utterly grateful to God for giving me such an incredible person to share my life with!”

Just two months after their engagement, TMZ ran photographs of the couple walking into New York City’s Marriage Bureau. The next day, People claimed that Hailey and Justin obtained their marriage license, officially making them husband and wife.

Meanwhile, Hailey dismissed the gossip on Twitter: “I understand where the speculation is coming from, but I’m not married yet!”

The couple finally confirmed their marriage status. Justin shared an Instagram photo of him and Hailey with the caption “My wife is awesome.” The following day, Hailey changed her last name to Bieber on all of her social media accounts.

TMZ broke the news that a second wedding was imminent after the date was moved several times. The outlet acquired a photo of a save the date card, which revealed that the ceremony would take place on September 30 in South Carolina.

Mr. and Mrs. Bieber officially tied the knot…again! People disclosed the details of their ceremony, which took place at Somerset Chapel in Bluffton, South Carolina. Vows (and Tiffany & Co. wedding bands) were exchanged “as the sun set.” The star-studded guest list included Kendall Jenner, Camila Morrone, and Jaden Smith, among others.

A day later, Justin basked in wedded bliss as he shared photos from the couple’s reception.

The Biebers continued to share photos from their big day. Hailey put her Off-White by Virgil Abloh wedding dress on full display, including her elaborate train, which read “’till death do us part.” Justin wore a Celine tuxedo.

Weeks later, the newlyweds found themselves embroiled in Jelena fan drama, after Justin’s ex dropped her new single “Lose You To Love Me.” The track captured Gomez’s feelings moving on from her 10-year on-off romance with Justin and closing that chapter.

Shortly after the song came out, Hailey upset some Jelena fans when she posted an Instagram Story, where she shared that she was listening to Summer Walker’s “I’ll Kill You.” Hailey denied that this was a dig at Gomez. Commenting beneath JustJared’s Instagram post, she wrote, “please stop with this nonsense. There is no ‘response.’ This is complete BS.”

Gomez, meanwhile, told her fans on Instagram Live not to attack Hailey. “I am grateful for the response that the song is getting. I’m so grateful,” she said. “However, I do not stand for women tearing women down. And I will never, ever be by that. So please be kind to everyone. It doesn’t matter what the situation is. If you’re my fans, don’t be rude to anybody, please. Don’t go off and say things that you just feel in the moment. And just please, from me, know that that’s not my heart. My heart is only to release things that I feel that are me and that I’m proud of. And that’s all that I’ll say, yeah.”

Hailey tried to shut down feud rumors herself when she liked Gomez’s Instagram post promoting “Lose You To Love Me.” A source close to the Biebers also assured E! that things were copacetic. “It isn’t ideal for Hailey,” the insider told the outlet, “but she understands the creative process of writing music and that Justin had a past. Justin and Hailey both want Selena to be happy and in a good place and aren’t fazed by it.”

Justin rang in the decade with his new single “Yummy,” which details his sex life with Hailey.

Hailey landed the March 2020 cover of ELLE. She spoke candidly about the couple’s decision to delay their South Carolina ceremony for a year. “When we first got married, we were just figuring out our life together,” she said. “I felt like putting a wedding in the middle of all of that would be really hectic and stressful.”

Although the Biebers weren’t ready for children yet, Hailey was already thinking about parenting. Amid worldwide protests in solidarity with Black Lives Matter, Hailey discussed her outlook on motherhood. Regarding her future children, she told Vogue India, “They will be raised knowing how to treat people, why we don’t say certain things, and why we respect and acknowledge and give credit where credit is due.”

The Biebers attended their first Met Gala as husband and wife. Hailey stunned in a Saint Laurent column gown and matching wayfarer sunglasses. Justin paired his sleek suit with customized Nike sneakers.

Hailey and Justin appeared on the In Good Faith with Chelsea & Judah Smith podcast, where they discussed the challenges they faced in their first year of marriage. At the time, Justin was battling with severe bouts of depression. Hailey admitted that watching her partner struggle wasn’t easy.

“There were days where I literally was like, ‘I don’t know if he’s going to be okay.’ Something really deep down inside of me was like, ‘He’s going to get through it.’ I just didn’t know how long it was going to take. That’s what I think was the hardest thing. There’s no guarantees,” she said.

Nevertheless, Hailey was determined to stick by her husband: “Imagine abandoning somebody in the middle of the worst time of their life, potentially. I’m not that type of person,” she said.

Amid the launch of her skin care line Rhode, Hailey did an interview with WSJ Magazine. The entrepreneur shared her thoughts on having children. “I think ideally in the next couple of years we would try. But there’s a reason they call it try, right?” she said. “You don’t know how long that process is ever going to take. Definitely no kids this year; that would be a little bit hectic, I think.”

Hailey also revealed her decision to stop discussing her marriage in interviews. “It doesn’t feel worth it to me anymore,” she explained. “I try to have an open conversation with someone, and then it gets taken out of context.”

Hailey was hospitalized after having stroke-like symptoms, though she fortunately fully recovered. Her health scare left Justin reasonably shaken, with a source close to the couple telling People, “[He] is probably more traumatized than even she is. When it happened, there was a lot of panic. Justin texted everyone he knew and asked everyone to pray for her, and he never left her side. He was saying that he can’t lose her, that whatever it takes, he wanted the best medical treatment available.”

Justin later discussed the situation during one of his concerts. “You know, it’s kind of crazy how life throws you curveballs,” he said during a Denver performance. “Most of you probably know or seen the news about my wife …but she’s okay, she’s good, she’s strong. It’s been really scary. But I know for a fact that God has her in the palms of his hands, and that’s a good thing.”

Hailey accompanied her husband at the Grammys. She opted for a flowy strapless gown, which led some fans to speculate that she was hiding a growing baby bump. After RadarOnline published an Instagram post about the rumors, Hailey swiftly shut them down. “I’m not pregnant; leave me alone,” she commented.

Just months after Hailey’s hospitalization, Justin had a health scare of his own. A virus called Ramsay Hunt syndrome left half of the singer’s face paralyzed, but he eventually recovered. A source told People that although this year has been “overwhelming” for the couple, relationship-wise, “they’re unbreakable.”

During an interview with Good Morning America, Hailey shared a promising update on her husband’s health. “He is getting better every single day. He’s feeling a lot better and, obviously, it was just a very scary and random situation to happen, but he’s going to be totally okay, and I’m just grateful that he’s fine,” she said.

Ahead of the couple’s fourth anniversary, Hailey discussed her relationship with Justin in Harper’s Bazaar. “[Justin’s] still the person that I wanna be rushing back to,” she said. “I might fly somewhere and go do a job, but I can’t wait to come back and hang out. And I feel like that’s because of the effort that’s been put in on both sides. At the end of the day, like, he’s my best friend, but it still does take a lot of work to make it work.”

Hailey appeared on the Call Her Daddy podcast. In a conversation with Alexandra Cooper, Hailey insisted that she never “stole” Justin from Gomez and that it’s “not [her] character to mess with someone’s relationship.” She also confirmed that Justin had already “closed a chapter” with Gomez before he rekindled things with her in 2018.

Hailey went on to discuss her seemingly speedy engagement to Justin, which took place just two months after they began dating again. “I’m like, ‘yeah, that seemed really drastic and really crazy,’” she said. “But that was what we felt was a decision between the two of us, and it felt correct for the two of us at the time, and clearly, we were right because here we are, four years later.”

Hailey and Gomez posed for pictures together at the Academy Museum Gala, proving once and for all that there is no drama between them. A source informed People about Justin’s reaction to the news. “[He’s] very happy with the fact that they can all move on and that it can be peaceful between everyone,” the source said.

Of Hailey and Gomez’s motivation, a source told Entertainment Tonight, “Selena and Hailey were both super chill together at the Academy Museum Gala. They’ve both moved on and are happy in their own lives. They wanted to show the world that there’s no beef or bad feelings between them anymore.”

A source gave Entertainment Tonight a brief update on Hailey and Justin’s relationship as 2022 closed out. “Hailey and Justin are doing incredible as a couple,” the source said. “They are each other’s rocks. They make sure they’re there for each other for whatever each of them needs and show their support for one another.”

“They have so much love and passion in their relationship and share the same beliefs and values, so it’s easy for them to get along,” the insider continued. “They love doing pretty much everything together, especially traveling.” The couple ended their year by traveling to Aspen and celebrating the start of 2023 with Kendall and Kylie Jenner.

Justin interviewed Hailey for Vogue Australia. He asked her what her favorite part of being married is. “Mmm... My favorite thing about being married is honestly the companionship I feel we have,” she said. “Genuinely, you are my best friend in the entire world. There’s nobody I would rather spend more time with or do anything with.”

Hailey posted a birthday tribute to Justin, ignoring the ongoing TikTok discourse

about her history with Gomez. She wrote to her husband, “29 never looked so good ☺️Happy Birthday to you best friend! Words couldn’t possibly sum up all that you embody. So here’s to more joy, more travel, yummy food, adventures, more peace, fun, and most of all more love. ✨🥳”

Justin didn’t comment on the TikTok drama but shared a tribute to Hailey to assert his love for her. “LUV U BABY,” he wrote.

Hailey and Gomez shared statements on March 24, asking for the fan bullying to stop. Hailey wrote:

The couple was regularly photographed out together during summer 2023.

On August 28, Justin went viral for wearing sweatpants while Hailey was in a red minidress at an event both attended to promote her Rhode Beauty and Krispy Kreme doughnut collaboration.

Justin then posted a couple of Instagrams featuring him and Hailey together. In one shot, he appears wearing a sweatshirt with her name on it while showing PDA with her.

The Biebers marked their fifth wedding anniversary with Instagram tributes.

Justin’s was longer. The singer wrote to Hailey, “To the most precious, my beloved. 5 years. You have captivated my heart. I know from the depths of my soul down to my bones that this journey with you will only exceed our wildest expectations. So let’s keep dreaming big baby. Cheers to forever and ever. #6581. Of Course Trump Found a Way to Plug His Big, Ugly Ballroom When Partaking in a Beloved Thanksgiving Tradition

The idea of turkeys in that Gilded Palace of Sin is just too damn on the nose.

(Alternative Musical Accompaniment to the Last Post of the Week from the Blog’s Favourite Living Canadian)

We’re battening down here for the predicted Thanksgiving Gale. (The famous Perfect Storm is known as the Halloween Gale. We name storms like that. We are fcking adorable that way.) Apparently, this mother is going to slam the entire northeast corridor from Washington to Maine. Which means massive chaos at a number of very busy airports. And given the performance of the secretary of transportation and the secretary of homeland security when a squirrel recently got into the wiring in El Dorado, Arkansas, I have never been more glad not to be traveling this weekend. At least we will be spared another goony-bird press conference from Sean Duffy and Markwayne Mullin, referred to by writer and musician David Ferguson immortally as Dumb and Plumber. That’s a keeper.

It’s going to be tough to fly, tougher to take a train, and even tougher than that to drive. And the storm is going to lock people indoors with their obnoxious relatives, which can only lead to alcoholic embarrassments and domestic mayhem. Of course, it always could be worse. We’re all being stuck in the house by the elements of the natural world, whereas the folks in Iowa and all over the Midwest are being gifted with a cornucopia of toxic clouds for the holiday. From The New York Times:

What’s worse? Being stuck in the house with Meemaw, who found the bourbon, or being stuck in the family van, heading south, with Meemaw, who found the bourbon? The Army’s got your back, Iowa, but pack a bag and scout out a route to Honduras anyway. Wow.

And I’m sure this last-minute FEMA warning didn’t confuse anyone.

Don’t just do something, dammit, stand there.

And not for nothing, but the Army’s been acting sketchy about this whole business almost from jump. From The Washington Post:

Did the president use the charming tradition of pardoning a turkey for Thanksgiving as an excuse for plugging his Gilded Palace of Sin? (Thanks, Gram.) What do you think? From Axios:

Turkeys in that ballroom are just too damn on the nose.

The 2026 midterm elections continue to bless us. Representative Scott DesJarlais, perhaps the worst human ever elected to the House of Representatives, is gone baby gone, beaten by Democratic candidate Victoria Broderick. DesJarlais’s rap sheet is nigh unprecedented. This all came out in 2012, and the voters kept sending this guy back to Washington by fat margins until two weeks ago. He lost to Broderick, a proudly pansexual 34-year-old mother of two whom he beat handily in 2024. However, since then, the Republican Tennessee legislature brilliantly redrew the maps, adding slices of Nashville to the Fourth Congressional District, a change that benefitted Broderick. So not only is Congress liberated from the likes of DesJarlais, but Broderick’s win was also another example of how Republican ratfcking of the redistricting process bit them on the ass. Heh, heh, heh.

Weekly WWOZ Pick to Click: “Happy Days” (McCoy Tyner): Yeah, I pretty much still love New Orleans.

Weekly Visit to the Pathé Archives: Here, from 1940, is FDR celebrating Thanksgiving with the patients at the Warm Springs polio facility where he once was a patient. The narrator makes a funny about the U.S. joining “the war” against polio. FDR chats up a young patient who is chowing down on a turkey leg that is as big as her head. It looks like it was fun to have a real president.

Discovery Corner: Hey, look what we found! From Live Science:

I have to say, a “floating castle” sounds like a terrible idea, and wearing chain mail on a floating castle sounds like an even worse one. If the floating castle blows up and sinks, then it’s fairly hard to swim in chain mail.

Old King Hans has come down as a jolly old soul, but he was quite the political schemer. He also died in one of those prosaic ways kings died in those days. He fell from his horse.

Hey, SciNews, is it a good day for dinosaur news? It’s always a good day for dinosaur news!

Once again, I point out that paleontology doesn’t necessarily require sweating over some limestone cliff face. Grab a sandwich and a soda and hit the drawers of the file cabinets in museum basements. Surprises like this make me happy they lived then.

In honor of the holiday, I will not close with the usual recitation of the nation’s woes. But do spare a thought for the people—and the cows, and the sheep—under the plume in the Midwest. Make sure, however, to be grateful for all those things that warm your heart and make all your lights shine. And all say amen.

#6579. Who Is Michelle Yeoh’s Husband, Jean Todt?

The motorsports executive has been linked to the Oscar-winning actress since 2004

Michelle Yeoh has spent decades bringing stories to the silver screen—with roles in hit films like Crazy Rich Asians and Wicked to the upcoming Blade Runner 2099—but her love life has a pretty remarkable story of its own.

The Oscar-winning actress married French businessman and former Ferrari CEO Jean Todt in 2023, nearly 19 years after he first proposed. The pair have been together since 2004, supporting each other through career milestones, international travels, and plenty of memorable moments along the way. But who is the man standing by one of Hollywood’s most accomplished actresses?

Ahead, everything you need to know about Yeoh’s husband, Jean Todt, including his career in motorsports, how the couple met, and their long-awaited wedding.

Todt was born on February 25, 1946, in Pierrefort, a commune in France’s South-Central region. He studied at École des Cadres School of Economics and Business in Paris. At 80 years old, he’s 16 years Yeoh’s senior.

Todt is best known for his work in motorsports, but his career actually began behind the wheel—or, more accurately, in the passenger seat. He started as a rally co-driver, a role he held from 1966 to 1981, before moving into the business and management side of racing.

From there, he went on to work with some of the biggest names in the industry. In 1981, he joined Peugeot as its director of racing before founding Peugeot Talbot Sport, where he helped the team secure multiple World Rally Championship titles. In 1993, he moved to Ferrari, eventually becoming the company’s general manager in 2004 and CEO in 2006, a position he held until 2008.

But his career didn’t end with Ferrari. In 2009, Todt was elected president of the Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA), the governing body for international motorsports, including Formula One. He held the position for 12 years, until 2021, and has also served as the United Nations secretary general's special envoy for road safety since 2015.

Yeoh and Todt’s love story began in Shanghai, China, in June 2004. Yeoh attended a Ferrari event, where she met Todt, who was then the company’s general manager. According to the couple’s wedding program, they first crossed paths on June 4, 2004, and Todt proposed less than two months later, on July 26. Yeoh said yes, beginning what would become a nearly two-decade engagement.

After nearly 19 years together, Yeoh and Todt finally tied the knot on July 27, 2023, in Geneva, Switzerland, surrounded by family and friends. Brazilian racing driver Felipe Massa first shared the news, posting photos from the celebration on social media. Todt later confirmed the marriage and called Yeoh the love of his life.

The couple’s wedding program included a sweet recap of their relationship, noting that they had met 6,992 days earlier. Yeoh also shared photos from the celebration on Instagram, writing, “19 years and YES!! we are married!!” The actress wore several looks for the occasion, including a champagne-colored gown, and celebrated with loved ones—including her new husband’s colleagues from the world of Formula One.

Todt has one son, Nicolas, from a previous relationship. Born on November 17, 1977, Nicolas has followed in his father’s footsteps, carving out his own career in motorsports. He is a racing manager and talent manager who has worked with some of the sport’s biggest names, including Charles Leclerc and Felipe Massa.

I’m what you might call a sneaker hoarder. But after building a capsule wardrobe I currently swear by, I’ve found that three pairs have become the foundation of most of my fall outfits: my black Adidas Superstars, which tap into the retro sneaker revival and rising noir sneaker trend I’m loving lately; my earth-toned Salomon XT-Whispers, perfect for an easy gorpcore moment; and my lilac Adidas x Wales Bonner Japan shoes, which add a subtle splash of color to neutral looks while complementing the rich hues in my autumn lineup. With those themes in mind, and inspired by some of this year’s most viral celebrity getups and standout street-style looks, I’ve gathered a quick guide to seven exciting sneaker outfits below.

Maybe you’re eager to invest in a new staple pair, or maybe you already have one of these favorites tucked away at the back of your closet. Either way, there’s plenty of fresh inspiration to copy and paste this season. Ahead, discover key pairs to shop (if you don’t already own them) and the chic pieces to wear with them.

Y2K icons like Vans and Converse are quietly making a comeback, stylishly co-signed by stars like Bella Hadid and Margot Robbie. Here, Robbie nails the cold-weather off-duty formula, swapping classic booties for black All Star high-tops to give her cozy gray polo, leather trench, and straight-leg jeans a more casual edge. A zesty red beanie completes the look, breaking up the muted tones.

By Anthropologie 100 Percent Brushed Cashmere Beanie

Even a few years after Adidas Sambas surged in popularity, the legendary indoor soccer-inspired shoe has cemented its status as a bona fide modern classic. Zoë Kravitz was recently spotted wearing a black-and-white pair while filming her new rom-com, Die Alive, in New York, styling them with flowy black trousers and a burgundy sweater and scarf. It’s a polished yet easygoing ensemble perfect for everything from bakery runs to overdue weekend catch-ups.

Saks Basic Cashmere Easy Crewneck Sweater

Hollister High-Rise Pleated Wide-Leg Pants

Or, as aforementioned, try switching up a neutral outfit with a colorful pair of kicks. As Jennifer Lawrence shows, an emerald- or forest-green sneaker feels just right for fall and winter, easily styled back to baggy jeans, a chunky turtleneck, and a navy coat.

The coolest outfits often hinge on contrast, mixing different textures, proportions, and aesthetics. This Paris Fashion Week showgoer went polished on top with a striped button-down and plaid blazer (also creating a nice pattern play) and sporty on bottom with classic track pants and chunky black Asics sneakers. An oversized denim tote introduces yet another interesting element.

Favorite Daughter The Dean Plaid Notch Lapel Blazer

Speaking of contrast, I love the idea of using a chunky sneaker to give tailored separates a cool, nonchalant feel. A relaxed-fit tuxedo blazer and drapey wide-leg trousers are a match made in street-style heaven when teamed with a boxy white tee and metallic trainers, like the celebrity-favorite New Balance 530s.

Banana Republic Factory Double Breasted Tuxedo Blazer

Lauren Ralph Lauren Pleated Stretch Jersey Wide-Leg Pant

PerfectWhiteTee Harley Cotton Boxy Crew Tee

Retro runner silhouettes, with their slim, streamlined uppers and slightly thicker soles, are another IYKYK trend to keep on your radar. Taking a cue from this Paris Fashion Week attendee, don’t be afraid to work traditionally spring-ready colors into your look: a baby-blue cable-knit sweater and soft yellow track jacket look lovely—and still feel relevant—alongside a chocolate-brown maxi skirt, matching sneakers, and a rich burgundy handbag.

Vineyard Vines Cashmere Cable Crewneck Sweater

Just like a go-to pair of low-profile kicks, a good ol’ graphic tee can be styled with just about anything in your closet—and it’s the kind of playful, sentimental piece that’ll spark joy every time you reach for it. For a unique combo, pair your favorite artist tee with sporty pieces like a nylon skirt and track jacket. An oversized briefcase-style bag adds a sleek touch.

Over the itty-bitty two-piece, the star layered a sheer cover-up from the Dolce & Gabbana Spring 1997 runway. #6569. Your December Horoscope by Zodiac Sign

We’re wrapping up the year with great momentum going into the new year.

December’s astrology helps you wrap the year up with some forward momentum! At the start of the month, the Sun continues its joyful journey through Sagittarius, putting you in a more adventurous mood and encouraging you to expand your horizons and perspective. It's a great time to get in a debate during a holiday dinner and stand up for what you believe in, but to also practice your active listening skills and remain open to the possibility that you could learn something from someone else. You’re zooming out and thinking more about the world around you and eager to soak up life’s experiences by trying new things and meeting new people.

You’re feeling all-or-nothing when it comes to love once Venus moves into Scorpio on December 4. For the next few weeks, Venus is retracing its steps that it took during the retrograde, so you might finally experience relief or turning points regarding some of your key relationships and contracts. This can help you navigate uncomfortable terrain in your close connections with honesty and vulnerability. You’re feeling funnier than normal once Mercury enters Sagittarius on December 6. When our communication planet moves through jokester Sagittarius, your conversations are a bit more playful but words can also sting from time to time. It’s easier to speak what’s on your mind in the moment and regret it later. You might also have a harder time finding a plan or strategy to reach certain goals, but right now you’re not meant to sort through the details. Focus on the big picture and soaking up new information and experiences instead. If you’re traveling, you might also deal with more snafus, so plan accordingly!

A New Moon in Sagittarius on December 8 helps you reconnect with a source of hope or optimism. Conversations feel expansive and information that you learn might inform your worldview in a new way. This energy is also helpful for reframing the way you speak to yourself and releasing limiting beliefs. You might find yourself eager to book some travel or sign up for a workshop to hone a skill or learn something new. You’re not afraid to set firm boundaries when Saturn stations direct in Aries on December 10. This will bring you back to July 26, the day the retrograde began. Similar themes and topics are resurfacing and asking you to be accountable for your own limitations or to set necessary boundaries with courage.

A few days later, on December 12, Neptune stations direct in Aries, helping you to dissolve your ego. This brings you back to July 7, and puts you in touch with certain topics and conversations that were a focus around then. You might feel more tender and sensitive, or feel a burst of creativity. This can help you channel your own creative energy for a higher purpose or ideal to make a positive impact in the collective. On the same day, Jupiter stations retrograde in Leo, bringing a crisis of faith. You could learn news or experience something that rattles your foundation or makes you question your own belief system. This can put you in a philosophical mood, asking you to reflect on whether you’re living in alignment with your beliefs. There might also be developments regarding teachers and mentors in your life, decisions about going back to school, or turning points regarding some of your goals and dreams.

The Sun enters Capricorn on December 21, marking the Winter Solstice in the Northern Hemisphere and the longest night of the year. From now on, the daylight will slowly begin to increase once again. But first, you must move through winter and preserve your precious energy in the process. This is not the time to overdo it or overextend yourself. It’s time to prune people, patterns, and situations from your life that extinguish your drive and essence instead of replenishing them. A Full Moon in Cancer on December 23, highlights your relationship with the past, primary caregivers, and security. There might be significant developments within your chosen family or perhaps you’re making a decision about where you live. People are in a more sentimental mood and the past can stir up major feelings and reflections. Be gentle with yourself and others.

The month wraps up with Mercury entering Capricorn on December 25, lending you a more structured approach to your ideas and communication style. You might find yourself navigating boundaries more or even find yourself speaking with a little more directness. There’s no need to sugarcoat to keep others comfortable, your time is limited and you’ve got things to do! This energy can be productive, help you problem solve, and stick with habits and plans that build toward your longterm success.

#6568. We Tried 6 Store-Bought Pumpkin Pies—These Are The Only 2 Worth Serving At Thanksgiving

A handful of things are non-negotiable at Thanksgiving. You need turkey, stuffing, cranberry sauce, and, of course, a slice of pie to round out your meal. And pumpkin pie is the undeniable star of the dessert table.

But sometimes you're strapped for time and have too much on your plate (pun intended) to whip something up from scratch. So we tried six different grocery store pumpkin pies to find the best store-bought shortcut. And our team's verdict was pretty unanimous, even if it’s a bit hard to hear: No premade pie will ever taste as good as a homemade one.

It primarily comes down to the crust. Frozen and pre-baked pies typically rely on vegetable-based fat instead of butter because they’re more affordable, reliable, and shelf-stable—but that comes at a cost. You not only miss out on the decadent, buttery taste, but the crusts can also leave an unpleasant film on your tongue.

That said, when you need to outsource to the grocery store, we found two options that will work in a pinch.

The pie that we’d feel most confident bringing to Thanksgiving dinner comes straight from the Whole Foods bakery department. That’s not to say it’s perfect, though. The crust is almost upsettingly pale, but it’s made with real butter and only a little bit of palm oil. And since it doesn’t leave a noticeable film and still lets the butter flavor shine, we’ll let this one slide.

Once you look past the crust’s color, this pie is solid overall. The filling is decadent, not too sweet, and creamy without being mushy. Whole Foods doesn’t shy away from the spices, either.

Senior Editor Samantha MacAvoy noted that the warming spices are nicely balanced, while Designer Alison Dominguez said, “The flavor was exactly how a pumpkin pie should taste.”

Costco’s pumpkin pie isn’t perfect: The crust uses palm oil-based shortening rather than butter and can develop a soggy bottom if you buy it too far in advance. (And it doesn’t hold a candle to the warehouse’s holy grail pumpkin cheesecake.) But it has a cult following for a reason, and not just because of its $5.99 price tag.

Even with its faults, the crust has great flavor and enough salt to create a balanced bite. Dominguez appreciated how it was “flaky and not too thick, and most importantly, it let the pie filling itself shine.” News and Features Editor Amanda Mactas chose Costco’s pie as her number one pick. “It all seemed to melt together in one creamy bite,” she said.

And at over three pounds, this dessert is the indisputable champion if you want to feed a crowd for less.

#6566. How Does Owen Wilson Find His Zen?

“I just believe there’s something more going on that you can tap into,” the actor tells Esquire on the latest episode of “What I’ve Learned.”

Every product was carefully curated by an Esquire editor. We may earn a commission from these links. Here’s how we test products and why you should trust us.

Owen Wilson is a spiritual guy—and long has been. That’s why it fits so naturally that he would star in a golf series for Apple TV, Stick, in which his character, Pryce Cahill, is often searching to find his perfect zen. And as Wilson jokes, he’s started calling himself “Johnny Flowstate” on the green as he talks to himself through shots.

“I just believe there’s something more going on that you can tap into,” he tells Esquire editor in chief Michael Sebastian on the latest episode of “What I’ve Learned.” The fifty-five-year-old actor, best known for his roles in The Royal Tenenbaums, Wedding Crashers, and Midnight in Paris, even admits that he found himself reaching into the beyond for advice from his late father, TV executive Robert Wilson, in a moment of pure panic before hosting Saturday Night Live in 2021.

“He was already gone at that point, but the night before I was freaking out like, I don’t know if I can do this. I was so nervous, and I was thinking a lot about my dad,” Wilson says. The two were incredibly close, and he reveals that his father actually worked with him and his brothers, actors Luke Wilson and Andrew Wilson, on several of their films. One of which was Wes Anderson’s Rushmore, in which their father wrote Bill Murray’s now-iconic church address to the students: “Take dead aim on the rich boys."

So, as Wilson found himself full of doubt and fear the night before hosting SNL, he recalls looking up and “literally asking [his father] for help” before falling asleep. “I woke up, just incredibly calm, and I had this conviction of this joke my dad would say that needed to go in my monologue.”

What was the joke? “That he was the charter member of the 3970 club,” Wilson says, “which stood for ‘three sons, nine high schools, seven colleges, and zero degrees.’”

“That wasn’t something he was proud of,” Wilson continues. “That was his way to cope with disappointment, but you could almost say that that joke was worth us having all those struggles in school because that joke has lived longer than another diploma would have.” You can watch the episode above as well as listen on Spotify and Apple Podcasts.

Luckily, it all worked out for the Wilson brothers. Next up, Owen is set to appear in season 2 of Stick on Apple TV and the Meet the Parents legacy sequel, Focker-in-Law with Ben Stiller. He also takes a liking to Esquire’s suggestion of a Christmas movie with another one of his longtime collaborators, Wes Anderson, in the episode.

“It’s one of the biggest relationships of my life,” Wilson says of his friendship with the director. “Had I gotten into one of the colleges that I applied to, I would never have met Wes. And there’s something I always say to my boys—the idea that you can’t do it alone. If there’s something going wrong, I know I can always call and he’ll always be there for me.”

#6565. 12 Last-Minute Thanksgiving Desserts For When One Pie Just Won't Cut It

Come Thanksgiving, there’s always an emphasis on mastering the turkey and the sides, but sometimes the desserts fall through the cracks. Not that I’m one to turn my nose at a store-bought pumpkin pie, but for a holiday as iconic as Thanksgiving, something a little more special is called for. So this year, if you find out last minute that the only dessert is a pecan pie somebody picked up from the supermarket, take it upon yourself to make the difference. These 12 last-minute Thanksgiving desserts are the perfect way to level up your holiday spread in a pinch. Plus, they’re all super cute.

This year, why settle for the usual when you could elevate your holiday game with a turkey sculpture made entirely out of Rice Krispies treats? Imagine the look on your guests' faces when you unveil your masterpiece, glistening with cinnamon-sugar goodness.

Turkey is the star of Thanksgiving dinner, but it can also be the star of dessert if you stretch your imagination enough. This idea first gained popularity on TikTok, using chocolate-dipped strawberries, marshmallows, pretzel rods, and melted chocolate to create these adorable little treats.

#6564. 50 Percent of People In Relationships Would Take a Trip Together to Solve Their Problems

We may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love. Promise.

A “baecation” often entails a romantic getaway, passionate activities, and a lot of vacation sex. But what if traveling with your significant other meant a lot of difficult conversations, a heated back-and-forth, and working to fix your relationship. I know: this sounds nothing like the dreamy R&R you pictured—but for some couples, it’s exactly what they planned for.

According to Booking.com’s 2027 Travel Predictions, 58 percent of U.S. travelers said they would consider taking a trip to resolve conflicts or arguments.

Now, traveling itself already can cause real strain and arguments on relationships on its own. In the same data set, more than one-third of respondents said they found out they were incompatible with their companion after a trip. Nearly three in 10 people have considered ending a relationship or friendship over a trip, while more than one in five have actually cut a vacation short because of a bad travel companion.

But if you’re already having relationship issues with your partner, is a trip a good idea? People still seem to think so. About 81 percent said that taking part in at least one vacation activity with another person helps them have honest or difficult conversations.

So should you be planning a trip the next time you and your partner start arguing?

A change of scenery might be exactly what you and your partner need to see eye-to-eye again.

“Getting away from work, chores, kids, in-laws, or house and childcare stuff can lower defenses,” couples therapist Justena Kavanagh tells Cosmopolitan.

She explains that when you’re home, you’re essentially having every argument on the same “battleground.”

“Somewhere new often brings back the honeymoon period, when you could really see each other without life’s stresses in the way,” she says. And if both you and your partner have busy lives and packed schedules, a vacation may really be the only time you can focus on the issues in your relationship without distraction.

Plus, vacations encourage you to relax—which can go a long when in an argument. “When we’re rested, we’re more regulated, and when we’re regulated, we can listen instead of defending,” Kavanagh says.

She explains that it’s important to establish why exactly you’re going on the vacation in the first place. Are you getting away to talk about an issue? Or simple to get away from it and reconnect? Agreeing on the purpose for the trip before you start packing your bikini will help you and your partner get on the same page—so you don’t end up just arguing more later.

“Trips suit conversations about connection, like feeling distant, intimacy, or where the relationship is going,” she says. Other things like finances or in-law conflicts may need a follow-up at home.

If you decide that you’re going to talk your issues out, remember that you are still on vacation. That doesn’t mean everything has to be wonderful, of course. But Kavanagh encourages couples to treat the trip like a summit. This means talking early in the day (after a good night’s rest) and working on things while taking breaks.

The trip should essentially be your opportunity to discuss what’s currently happening in the relationship, where you want the relationship to go, and how to shift priorities to get there.

Sure, a beautiful view and hotel sex will definitely lighten the mood and probably even make you more agreeable—but it isn’t a magical bandaid for your relationship issues.

“If couples don’t have relational skills at home, they won’t miraculously have them on vacation,” Kavanagh warns.

So if you’re going to go on a vacation to work on things with your partner, you’re going to want to put a plan into place. The best method? Talking about the pattern behind the argument, rather than hyperfocusing on the latest incident.

And even if you do come to a resolution on vacation, make sure you’re setting a plan in place for the positive energy to flow into your everyday lives.

“Be realistic about home, where you’re more stressed and old patterns return fast,” Kavanagh says. “Plan follow-up support, a regular check-in, and what you’ll do when things go off track, because they will.”

Okay, so not all of us can afford to book a flight every time we get into an argument with our partner—but you don’t have to. Out of all the activities that people do on vacation, respondents said that it was mostly hikes or walking that was the most effective at getting them to open up and have the difficult conversations.

Lucky for you, taking a hike is totally free—and can do wonders for whatever issue you may be facing with your partner.

Kavanagh explains that walking and hiking take pressure off of an argument.

“Face to face can feel like a confrontation; side by side, you’re facing the same direction and don’t have to hold eye contact in the hardest moments,” she explains. This is something we see in psychotherapy: think about someone lying on a couch, looking at the ceiling. This helps physiologically and emotionally. Plus the actual physical activity helps, too.

“Walking also discharges stress and is a natural form of bilateral stimulation, the left-right rhythm used in therapies like EMDR,” she says.

When your partner is irritating you, it’s likely that the last thing you want to do is travel with them. But if you’re determined to move past whatever may be causing a rift, that might be exactly what you need.

Honeymoons and other happy occasions shouldn’t be the only time we travel with our partners with the purpose of growing closer, reconnecting, and strengthening the relationship. Sometimes, even in hardship, a little getaway could be the jumpstart your relationship needs to get back on track. Just remember that after the vacation ends, you do have to go back to reality.

“The good feelings are real, but the test is whether they last back home, where life is harder,” Kavanagh says.
